answer.reasons: I would put this on air as delivered. It is a clean, slim scorebug in the top-left corner: team names on solid club-colour bands, a dark score column and a dark clock block with an orange quarter label. Everything reads well over both the dark and the light backgrounds. The long accented French names stay inside the same strip width: one wraps to two lines and the other shrinks slightly, with no clipping and no overflow. Every action the brief asks for is on the operator surface and shows up in the frames: the clock runs after start (9:59, then 9:51) and holds after stop, the interval shows MI-TEMPS with the clock dimmed, full time shows FIN, and the score bumps update correctly. The intro and exit animations are clean. My only reservations are small: the wrapped long name is set noticeably smaller than the other team's name, and the sizes shift a little between states.

answer.reasons: There are no basic mistakes. Nothing overlaps, the kicker is readable on all three grounds, and Take and Out animate cleanly. As a designer, though, I would not put it on air. Each logo is shut inside its own box, and the boxes don't match: a dark, gold-outlined box for the white logo and cream boxes for the other two. The full-colour square mark ends up as a square in a box in a strip. Together this reads as patched-together tiles, not a designed sponsor strip that keeps the logos visible. The kicker also does not change when the Update sends its long value.

otherProblems: Each partner logo sits on a plate of its own instead of on the maroon strip, so the logos read as three boxed-in cards rather than as part of one design (G-2, G-5, G-27 to G-30).

The plates don't match. The white logo gets a near-black plate with a gold outline, while the other two get cream plates with no outline. The first tile looks highlighted or selected, as if it were a UI state, and not like an equal partner (G-2, G-3, G-4, G-28).
The square full-colour mark looks small and lost in the middle of a wide cream plate next to the wider wordmarks, so the logos don't look the same size (G-2, G-30).
There is a large empty stretch of maroon between the kicker and the first logo tile, which leaves the strip unevenly balanced (G-2).
answer.reasons: There are no basic mistakes. The kicker is clean and readable on every background, nothing clips or overlaps in the stress frames, and Take, Update and Out all play cleanly. The strip still doesn't air. It solves the white-logo and black-logo problem by putting every logo on its own plate. With the small square mark floating in its wide plate, the strip looks like a row of mismatched cards on a band and not like one designed 'supported by' strip.

otherProblems: Each partner logo sits on a plate of its own (G-2 to G-7): a dark tile with a gold outline for the white logo and flat cream tiles for the black and full-colour logos. The logos read as pasted-in boxes rather than part of the maroon strip.

The three plates don't match. The first is near-black with a gold keyline and the other two are cream with no outline, so the first tile looks highlighted or selected rather than designed as part of the row (G-2, G-5, G-27 to G-30).
The logos are small inside wide plates. With the long values (the shield marks in G-5 and G-28/G-29) each logo fills only a small part of its tile, so the plates look mostly empty.

The Update of the Kicker to its long value (G-17 to G-21) makes no visible change to the strip.
answer.reasons: There are no basic mistakes. Nothing overlaps or gets clipped, the kicker reads clearly on the maroon, and the Take and Out animations are clean. All three logos stay visible on every ground. The way it keeps them visible is the problem: each logo gets its own boxed plate, and the plates don't match (one dark with a gold outline, two cream). The first one looks selected and the row looks like three stuck-on boxes rather than one designed strip. The small marks in wide plates and the large empty band when there are no logos add to that. It needs a design pass before it goes on air.

otherProblems: With an empty label value (G-6, G-7) the red CAMPUS block stays on screen as an empty red slab. The brief fixes the label, so this is unlikely on air, but the block should collapse when it has nothing in it.
The soft red glow around the label block is a little heavy on the dark plate. It is still acceptable.
Mid-transition (G-44) the strip briefly shows an empty dark bar between items. This is normal for a crossfade, and the next item follows straight after.
answer.reasons: This airs. It is a clean ticker strip: a red CAMPUS block next to a dark bar, with white sentence-case items that read well on both the video ground and the light ground. Long items with Finnish street names (Yliopistonkatu, Hämeenkatu, Kauppakorkeakoulunkatu) are never cut off and never run under the label. The bar grows to two lines and the text stays inside its padding. Pause holds the current item, Resume starts the cycle again, and Skip moves to the next item with a tidy fade-and-slide. Take and Out are smooth. The only weak point is the empty red block in the empty-label case, which is minor because the label is a fixed brand element.

otherProblems: With empty values (G-6, G-7) the red label tab is shown as a bare red block with no text. This only happens if the operator clears the fixed 'CAMPUS' label, so it is minor.
When an item wraps to two lines (G-13, G-25, G-31), the strip grows upward and the label recentres. It stays clean, but the strip's height changes from item to item.
The label has a soft red glow. It is restrained, though some would leave it out.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, simple ticker. A solid university-red 'CAMPUS' tab sits flush against a dark strip, with large white sentence-case text that reads well over both the video and the light backgrounds. Long items, including the Finnish street names, wrap onto a second line inside the strip. They are never cut off and never run under the label. Skip, pause and resume all behave as the brief asks: a paused item holds at 10 s, and resume and skip move on to the next item with a clean crossfade. The Take and Out are simple fades. Only small nits remain, none of which would keep it off air.

otherProblems: With the label field emptied (G-6, G-7) the red label block stays up empty. The brief fixes the label as CAMPUS, so in normal use no viewer would see this.
The longest item wraps to two lines and the strip grows taller (G-13, G-30). That is unusual for a ticker but clean, and it keeps the text whole.
Resume after Pause moves straight on to the next item (G-42 to G-46) rather than holding the current one a little longer. That is a small behaviour nit.
answer.reasons: G would go on air. It is a clean bottom strip with a red CAMPUS label block next to a dark text band. The white text reads well on both the dark and the light ground, and the padding and alignment are even. The long items with Finnish street names are never cut off and never run under the label: the single long line fits inside the band, and the longest one wraps neatly onto a second line as the strip grows, still clear of the label. The operator surface offers pause, resume and skip, and the frames show each one working: Pause holds the item at 10 s, Next brings in a new item, and Resume starts the cycle again. The fades in and out are clean. The only flaw is the empty red block when the label is cleared, and the brief rules that state out.

Removing the badge leaves a hole at the top of the panel. In a near tie, the winner is shown only by a gold tint on one row, with dull grey bars for the others. A director would send this back.

otherProblems: The footer still reads '6,008 VOTES · VOTING OPEN' after Close voting (G-18/G-19), on the result (G-24/G-25) and on the winner call (G-51/G-52). The status line tells the hall and the stream that voting is open when it is closed.

Closing voting removes the VOTE NOW badge and leaves an empty band at the top of the panel (G-18, G-24, G-51). The question then sits low under a lot of dead space, and the top padding looks broken.

The winner call is weak for a 40.2% vs 39.7% finish. The winning name and figure just turn gold, there is no winner label, and the other bars change to a muddy grey-brown that looks out of place in the navy and gold palette (G-51).
answer.reasons: The panel itself is tidy: navy and gold, readable type, and long names and the long question fit cleanly with no collisions or clipping. It still shouldn't go to air. After the operator closes voting, the footer keeps saying 'VOTING OPEN' through the result and the winner call, which is plainly wrong on screen. The bars stay empty for the whole live vote even though the brief asks for bars that grow as people vote. Removing the badge also leaves a hole at the top of the panel. The winner call for a very close finish is a subtle colour change with no winner label.

otherProblems: The footer still reads '6,008 VOTES · VOTING OPEN' after Close voting, after Show result and after Call the winner (G-19, G-25, G-52). The board contradicts itself on air.

While voting is open, all three bars stay empty even with 6,008 votes counted (G-2, G-13). The brief asks for bars that grow as the audience votes, but they only fill after Show result, so the live board looks broken.
When Close voting removes the VOTE NOW badge, nothing replaces it. A large empty band is left at the top of the panel and the padding becomes uneven (G-19, G-25, G-52).

The winner call is weak for a close race. The winning name and percentage just turn gold and there is no winner label. The losing bars change to a muddy taupe that looks like a mistake rather than a deliberate dimmed state (G-52).
answer.reasons: The panel itself is clean: midnight blue and gold, readable type, and the Swedish and Spanish names fit with nothing colliding. It still fails as a live vote board. The bars never move while voting is open. After the operator closes voting, the footer still says VOTING OPEN, and it says so through the result and the winner call too. Closing also pulls the badge and leaves an empty gap at the top. The winner call barely sets the winner apart and turns the other bars a muddy colour. A director would send it back.

Celebrate and settle both work, the celebrate state looks clearly different, and the card settles back after it. But the card with the brief's own values never shows the winner's crest, which the brief specifically asks for. When the crest does appear, it sits on a heavy white roundel plate that fights the black-and-orange design rather than belonging to it. A director would send it back for the crest treatment before putting it on air.

basicMistakes.where: The settled card with the brief's own values has no winner's crest anywhere. The crest is also missing from every Take, Celebrate and Settle frame (G-12, G-19, G-25, G-46).

The crest shown is a navy placeholder shield, not the black and dark orange crest the brief describes, so the frames never show the brief's own concern about a dark crest vanishing into the card being solved.
In the Celebrate state (G-17 to G-19) the widened orange bands leave black wedges in the top-left and bottom-right corners of the frame, which look like gaps rather than design.
With sample values the content block sits high and leaves a large empty black area across the lower third of the full-frame card.
answer.reasons: I would not air this as delivered. The type is clean and readable: the Finnish letters (Ä, Å, Ö) render correctly, the long values fit without clipping, and both Celebrate and Settle are offered and work. But the brief asks for the winner's crest, and the card with the brief's own values never shows one in any state. The only crest appears in the long-value frames, and there it is a navy placeholder on a white plate of its own. So the requirement that a black and dark-orange crest must stay visible on the card is never shown working. Celebrate also leaves black wedges at the frame corners that look accidental.

otherProblems: With the long values (G-4/G-5, G-26–G-30), the Swedish title fits on one line but its block keeps its two-line height. That leaves a gap of about 135 px between it and the English line, against about 50 px with the sample values, so the vertical rhythm loosens.

Take and Out are a plain fade or cut. That's fine for a holding screen.

The bright white-and-gold star logo sits clearly on the dark ground with a soft glow. The Swedish title wraps cleanly, the English line is in gold italic, and the spaced service-name line and a large countdown follow. No text collides with anything, and all of it is easy to read. The long values fit inside the frame. Pause visibly holds the clock by dimming the digits, and Resume carries on counting down. The only blemish is the extra gap under a one-line long title, which a viewer would see but which still reads as breathing room rather than a broken layout.

otherProblems: With the long values (G-4/G-5, G-26–G-30) the title field keeps a fixed two-line height. When the title fits on one line it leaves a gap of about 120 px above the English line, so the vertical rhythm is uneven.
The long English line in G-4/G-44 stops at 'Welcome to the Christmas Midnight' with no ellipsis. It fits inside its field, but text seems to be dropped silently.
The paused state only dims the clock digits. It is subtle, but it is a clear enough cue for a holding screen.
answer.reasons: G would air. It is a calm, centred full-frame holding screen in deep blue with a gold accent. The white and gold star logo shows clearly on the dark ground, sits centred above the text and has no plate of its own. The bilingual title, the service name and a large countdown are all easy to read on every frame and both grounds. Pause and resume are on the operator surface and work: the clock dims and holds at 5:00, then starts counting down again. The Take and Out are clean fades. otherProblems: With the long values (G-4, G-5, G-30) the Swedish title fits on one line, but the space for a second line stays reserved. That leaves a noticeably larger gap between the title and the English line than in the sample layout.
The long English line ends on "…Christmas Midnight" with no ellipsis, so if the value was shortened, the viewer can't tell. It ends on a whole word and nothing is cut mid-glyph.
answer.reasons: This is a calm, centred full-frame holding screen in deep blue with candle-gold touches. It shows the logo, the bold white Swedish title, the gold italic English line, a short gold rule, the spaced-caps service name and a large countdown. Everything reads cleanly on the dark ground. The white and gold star logo sits on its own with a soft glow and no box or plate, and it is in proportion to the text. The long Swedish title, the long service name and the stress logo all stay inside the frame without any clipping or overlap. Pause dims the clock and Resume brings it back and keeps it counting, so the operator steps work. The Take and Out are clean fades. The only flaw is the extra gap left under a one-line long title, which is a minor spacing issue rather than a broken layout.

otherProblems: With the long race name (G-4, G-5, G-32 to G-36) the panel widens to about 760 px. The time stays left-aligned, so roughly the right half of the yellow band is empty. It reads as deliberate left alignment, but the band looks under-filled.
The race name wraps onto a second line at the hyphen in 'Cross-Country'. It stays clean and inside its black band, but the long state is noticeably taller and wider than the sample state.
answer.reasons: This graphic would air as delivered. It is a clean top-right clock: a black title band with a hazard-stripe edge, over a yellow band with very large heavy black digits, in the sporty yellow and black the brief asks for. The time is easy to read on a phone, and it reads well over both the dark and the light background. The long Finnish race name wraps to two lines inside its band without clipping or overlapping anything. Start counts up (00:01, then 00:09), Stop holds the time, Reset returns it to 00:00, and the Take, Update and Out transitions are clean. The only thing a designer might pick at is the empty yellow space to the right of the time when the panel widens for a long name, and that does not keep it off air.

otherProblems: With the long race name (G-4, G-5, G-36) the panel grows to about 760 px wide, but the clock stays left-aligned at the same size. That leaves roughly 360 px of empty yellow to the right of the time, so the bottom band looks a little lopsided.
The long title breaks at the hyphen in 'Cross-Country'. It reads fine but isn't an ideal line break.
answer.reasons: This would go on air as delivered. It's a clean, readable count-up clock in the top right: white race name on a black band, and a very large black MM:SS time on yellow that you can easily read on a phone. Yellow and black with a hazard-stripe top edge fits the sporty brief, and it holds up on both the video and light backgrounds. otherProblems: With the long race name the panel widens to about 760 px, and the left-aligned time leaves roughly the right half of the yellow band empty (G-4, G-5, G-36). It reads as a bit lopsided, though both rows share the same left edge.

answer.reasons: This would air. It's a clean top-right clock: a black title band under a yellow-and-black hazard stripe, over a solid yellow band with very large heavy black MM:SS digits that read easily on a phone. It looks sporty and stays readable on both the dark and light backgrounds. The long race name wraps onto two lines inside the band with nothing clipped or overlapping. Start counts up (00:01, 00:09), Stop holds the time, Reset returns it to 00:00, and the Take and Out transitions are clean. The only thing a viewer might notice is the empty yellow to the right of the time when the panel widens for a long name, and that still looks intentional rather than broken.
